free_tier.stated: A public, unauthenticated feed of scene release names with relative timestamps ('5 mins', '6 mins'), newest first.
free_tier.notes: No account, query cap or price appears on the page served.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: names and timestamps, not bytes

retention.stated: not stated; the front page lists only the most recent releases

egress.terms: Nothing is downloadable: the site publishes release names and times, not files.

interface_detail: A web listing. /about and /api both return nginx 404 on the origin, so no documented API exists at those paths.
tooling: Browser only as read. A crawler can parse the front page; there is no documented API to call.
chaining: The 'does this exist yet' layer: it answers whether a named release is real and how old it is, before a client spends a debrid pull on a search. Pairs with a torrent indexer (which release to fetch) or a DDL index (which post to look for).

limits.value: unstated; the origin answered a plain read with HTTP 403 and the content still rendered

binding_note: A name index transfers nothing, so no byte constraint binds.

identity_cost.detail: No account on the page served.

reliability_note: The origin returned HTTP 403 to the reader while still serving the listing through it, so a client that trusts status codes alone will record this site as blocked when it is not.
confidence_note: The listing was read today with releases minutes old. The 403-with-content behaviour is the same observation, and it is why the confidence note says 'served' rather than 'reachable'.

evidence.proved: the live release feed with '5 mins' / '6 mins' timestamps, and the upstream 403 that still returned content
no documented API at /api: the origin returns '404 Not Found' from nginx

notes: Named in the aggregators lane's Seen list. It is a pre database, so it belongs in the chain that decides what to fetch, not in the set of things that store bytes.
